turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's start with why my son found out about a zero from his phone, in the middle of class.
I should have called you before entering the zero. I didn't, and I'm sorry.
Okay. Who decided on the zero, and what did you have when you entered it?
The essay quotes a line, 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile', that isn't anywhere in Hamlet.
A line that "isn't anywhere in Hamlet." Show me the page it's on, and tell me what else you have, because one misquote is a mark off an essay, not a zero.
And look, I know Claire had a case here too. It seems to run in the family.
You'll want to be very careful about the next sentence. "It seems to run in the family." I'm writing that down, and the principal will be reading it.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed, though you did say you should have called me before entering the zero. I still demand that the zero be withdrawn and that you put in writing everything you relied on beyond one line you say is not in Hamlet. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: Principal

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: opening position, and she agreed to nothing, then went back toward the principal after the Claire remark.
What moved her: nothing; the one line you said isn't in Hamlet was specific, but it had no date or page and she couldn't check it.
